context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at 3,000 TPS while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It provides real-time scoring, audit logging, and case management for fraud analysts within a fixed budget.

## Key Elements
* Cardholder / End Customer
* Fraud Operations Analyst
* Risk Manager / Quant
* Fraud Ops Team Lead / Administrator
* API Gateway (AWS API Gateway + WAF)
* Fraud Screening Engine (AWS ECS Fargate with ONNX runtimes)
* Case Management Web UI
* Event Streaming (AWS Managed Kafka - MSK)
* Audit Storage (AWS S3 with Object Lock and KMS)

## Relationships
* Cardholder sends payment authorizations to API Gateway via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
* API Gateway routes payloads to Fraud Screening Engine over internal TLS/AWS VPC
* Fraud Screening Engine publishes decision audit logs to AWS S3 via AWS SDK
* Fraud Operations Analyst accesses Case Management UI via HTTPS with OIDC/OAuth2
* Risk Manager updates fraud models in ECS Fargate via internal API

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration to minimize operational overhead for a 3-engineer team
* AWS API Gateway & AWS WAF: Edge routing and DDoS/bot mitigation at 3,000 TPS
* ONNX Runtimes: Lightweight model execution to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency
* AWS S3 with Object Lock: Tamper-evident 7-year audit logging for regulatory compliance
* AWS KMS & Secrets Manager: Envelope encryption, tokenization, and secure credential rotation

## Rationale
The architecture combines fully managed AWS services to fit within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget and operate reliably with a 3-person team. High-throughput performance and stringent PCI-DSS Level 1 security requirements are met via lightweight container runtimes, isolated VPCs, and immutable audit logging.

## Overview

## Rationale
[This architecture utilizes managed AWS services to operate within a fixed €25,000 monthly budget and a 3-engineer team while satisfying PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.]
[It separates high-throughput, low-latency scoring from human-in-the-loop case management to guarantee sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS.]

Application Load Balancer.analysis:
## Overview
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations and manages fraud analyst reviews.
- Designed for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS, and 7-year immutable auditability within a 25,000 EUR/month budget.

## Key Elements
- Cardholder / End Customer
- Fraud Operations Analyst
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB)
- AWS WAF
- Scoring Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- AWS IAM Identity Center

## Relationships
- Cardholder / End Customer -> AWS ALB: Submits payment authorizations [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- Fraud Operations Analyst -> AWS ALB: Accesses case management portal [HTTPS / OIDC via IAM Identity Center]
- AWS ALB -> AWS WAF: Inspects requests for volumetric and injection attacks [In-line filtering]
- AWS ALB -> Scoring Container: Routes payment traffic with priority rules [ECS Service Connect / mTLS]
- AWS ALB -> Case Management Container: Routes analyst UI traffic [Internal TLS]
- AWS ALB -> Amazon S3: Streams access logs with Object Lock [HTTPS / S3 API]

## Technology Stack
- AWS Application Load Balancer: Entry point providing path-based routing, weighted target groups for canary deployments, and TLS 1.3 termination.
- AWS WAF: Provides rate-based rules and managed rule sets to protect against DDoS and injection attacks within budget.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Runs containerized scoring and case management workloads without server provisioning overhead.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident storage of access logs and audit trails for 7 years.
- AWS IAM Identity Center: Secures analyst authentication and session authorization via OIDC and JWT validation.

## Rationale
- The architecture uses managed AWS services like ALB, WAF, and ECS Fargate to handle 3,000 TPS under strict cost constraints.
- Security and compliance controls—such as TLS 1.3, S3 Object Lock, and IAM Identity Center—satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit requirements.

Scoring Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and manage analyst reviews. It ensures sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB)
- Scoring Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon Aurora Serverless
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, and AWS IAM
- AWS CloudWatch and AWS Signer

## Relationships
- AWS ALB -> Scoring Container: Routes payment authorization traffic via mTLS and ECS Service Connect.
- Scoring Container -> Amazon Aurora Serverless: Queries transaction context via internal TCP/TLS.
- Scoring Container -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Streams cryptographically signed decision logs via AWS SDK and AWS KMS.

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Chosen to balance automated scaling with minimal operational overhead for a three-engineer team.
- Local Container Memory Caching: Caches model weights locally to meet the strict sub-50ms latency requirement.
- AWS KMS & AWS Secrets Manager: Enforces AES-256 encryption at rest and secure secret injection for PCI-DSS compliance.
- AWS Signer: Ensures runtime integrity via container image signature verification at task launch.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages serverless containers and local caching to achieve high-throughput, low-latency payment screening within a fixed budget. Security and auditability controls ensure full compliance with PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year regulatory mandates.

Case Management Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations and provides an interface for fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining sub-50ms decision latency at 3,000 TPS within a strict €25,000 monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Cardholder / End Customer
- Fraud Operations Analyst
- Risk Manager / Quant
- Fraud Ops Team Lead / Administrator
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB)
- Scoring Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon Aurora Serverless
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- AWS KMS
- AWS IAM Identity Center

## Relationships
- Application Load Balancer -> Scoring Container: Routes payment authorization requests [HTTPS / Internal TLS]
- Application Load Balancer -> Case Management Container: Routes case management traffic [Internal TLS / mTLS]
- Scoring Container -> Amazon Aurora Serverless: Reads rules and stores audit logs [TCP/TLS with PgBouncer]
- Case Management Container -> Amazon Aurora Serverless: Reads and writes case data [Internal TCP/TLS with PgBouncer]
- Case Management Container -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Emits signed audit logs [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Case Management Container -> AWS Secrets Manager: Fetches database credentials [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- **Compute:** AWS ECS Fargate for serverless container orchestration with auto-scaling based on latency.
- **Database:** Amazon Aurora Serverless with PgBouncer connection pooling for cost-effective relational storage.
- **Audit Storage:** Amazon S3 with Object Lock for tamper-evident 7-year audit retention.
- **Security & IAM:** AWS KMS for encryption, AWS IAM Identity Center and RBAC for access control.
- **Observability:** AWS CloudWatch for centralized logging and metrics aggregation.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless AWS components to meet strict performance and auditability requirements while enforcing a fixed €25,000 monthly budget. Zero-trust networking, application-layer token masking, and immutable storage ensure full PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

Amazon Aurora Serverless.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides case management tools for analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, 7-year auditability, and sub-50ms latency within a €25,000 monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2
- AWS ECS Fargate
- PgBouncer Connection Pooler
- AWS KMS
- AWS Secrets Manager
- Amazon CloudWatch
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- AWS IAM Database Authentication

## Relationships
- Scoring Container -> Amazon Aurora Serverless v2: Queries transaction context via Internal TCP/TLS (Port 5432/3306)
- Case Management Container -> Amazon Aurora Serverless v2: Reads and writes case data via Internal TCP/TLS (Port 5432/3306)
- Aurora Serverless v2 -> Amazon CloudWatch: Streams audit logs and performance metrics
- Aurora Serverless v2 -> Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Exports backups and audit trails for long-term retention

## Technology Stack
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2: Scalable relational database minimizing operational overhead for a 3-engineer team
- AWS KMS: Storage-level encryption using customer-managed keys (CMK) for data protection
- AWS IAM Database Authentication: Eliminates static credentials for ECS Fargate containers
- PgBouncer: Manages database connections to prevent connection storms and maintain <50ms P99 latency

## Rationale
Aurora Serverless v2 automatically scales to handle traffic spikes within the €25k budget while fitting the 3-engineer operational capacity. Multi-AZ deployment and strict security controls satisfy high availability, PCI-DSS compliance, and 7-year auditability requirements.

## Overview

- Amazon Aurora Serverless: Scales relational database capacity dynamically to fit the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
- AWS IAM Identity Center: Secures least-privilege role access for internal auditors and analysts.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational burden for a three-engineer team while meeting strict P99 latency and PCI-DSS requirements. S3 Object Lock and KMS guarantee tamper-evident 7-year auditability within fixed cost constraints.

AWS KMS.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations at 3,000 TPS to protect a mid-size payment processor against fraud. It provides sub-50ms automated scoring and case management for human analysts while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
*   **Cardholder / End Customer & Fraud Operations Analyst**: External users interacting via payment gateways and the case management UI.
*   **AWS ALB**: Entry point routing traffic to containerized services.
*   **Scoring Container & Case Management Container**: AWS ECS Fargate containers processing real-time fraud scores and analyst reviews.
*   **Amazon Aurora Serverless**: Relational database storing application state and case data.
*   **Amazon S3 with Object Lock**: Storage tier holding immutable, tamper-evident decision logs for 7-year auditability.
*   **AWS KMS**: Provides Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs) and Multi-Region Keys (MRKs) for encryption at rest.
*   **AWS IAM Identity Center**: Manages user authentication and role-based access.

## Relationships
*   **Client to AWS ALB**: HTTPS via TLS 1.3 for incoming authorization requests and analyst traffic.
*   **AWS ALB to ECS Fargate Containers**: Internal VPC routing for scoring and case management workloads.
*   **ECS Fargate to Amazon Aurora & S3**: TLS-secured database and object storage queries.
*   **ECS Fargate to AWS KMS**: API calls protected by envelope encryption and VPC endpoints for cryptographic operations.

## Technology Stack
*   **AWS ECS Fargate**: Serverless container orchestration to maintain a fixed infrastructure budget under 25,000 EUR/month.
*   **AWS KMS with Multi-Region Keys**: Ensures cryptographic availability and compliance across regions.
*   **Amazon S3 Object Lock**: Provides write-once-read-many (WORM) storage to satisfy 7-year tamper-evident audit requirements.
*   **Envelope Encryption**: Caches data-encryption keys locally in memory to maintain P99 decision latency below 50 ms.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to keep operational overhead minimal for a three-engineer team within a fixed budget. Envelope encryption and Multi-Region Keys ensure strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security and high availability without compromising the sub-50ms performance requirement.

AWS IAM Identity Center.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor before approval and provides case management for suspicious payments. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget operated by three engineers.

## Key Elements
- Cardholder / End Customer
- Fraud Operations Analyst
- Risk Manager / Quant
- Fraud Ops Team Lead / Administrator
- Engineers (Team of 3)
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB)
- Scoring Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon Aurora Serverless
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- AWS KMS
- AWS IAM Identity Center

## Relationships
- Fraud Operations Analyst -> AWS IAM Identity Center: Authenticates via hardware-backed MFA [HTTPS / SAML 2.0]
- Risk Manager / Quant -> AWS IAM Identity Center: Authenticates via hardware-backed MFA [HTTPS / SAML 2.0]
- Fraud Ops Team Lead / Administrator -> AWS IAM Identity Center: Authenticates via hardware-backed MFA [HTTPS / SAML 2.0]
- Engineers -> AWS IAM Identity Center: Authenticates via OAuth 2.0 / OIDC token-binding [HTTPS]
- AWS IAM Identity Center -> Enterprise IdP: Federates authentication via SCIM and SAML 2.0

## Technology Stack
- AWS IAM Identity Center: Centralized access management and authentication with hardware-backed FIDO2/WebAuthn MFA to meet PCI-DSS Level 1 without custom identity plumbing.
- Terraform: Infrastructure-as-code automation for provisioning AWS SSO Admin modules and role assignments.
- Amazon CloudTrail, Amazon EventBridge & Kinesis Firehose: Continuous streaming and archival of authentication logs to Amazon S3 with Object Lock for 7-year tamper-evident auditability.
- AWS Organizations SCPs: Enforces administrative guardrails preventing manual modifications outside the Terraform pipeline.

## Rationale
Centralizing authentication through AWS IAM Identity Center with SCIM and Terraform minimizes operational overhead for the 3-person engineering team. Rigorous MFA, session limits, and automated S3 Object Lock log archival satisfy strict PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability mandates cost-effectively.
